about: Load-bearing prose claims of this package, each bound to a machine-checkable fact about the package. Run: python3 verification/verify_claims.py. The failure mode this exists to catch is ASSERTED + UNBACKED: the documents say it, the package does not do it.

claims.claim: The prediction register is cryptographically (GPG) signed; predictions are signed before their data are released.

detect.exclude_note: Meta-documentation about this very checker necessarily quotes the false claim it detects (e.g. when describing the negative control). Excluded for the same reason CHANGELOG.md is excluded from count claims: it is a record *about* claims, not an assertion. Noted honestly rather than silently hedged — the tool flagged its own documentation on first run.
detect.unless_note: Hedges fall into three families: (a) explicit self-correction (overstat/was false/v12.3), (b) explicit non-execution (not yet/never/unexecuted/not GPG-signed), (c) normative or definitional statements of the protocol rather than assertions about this register ('must be', 'or equivalent', 'is one whose'). Family (c) is the subtle one: a protocol spec may legitimately describe signing it does not perform. Validated empirically: these hedges still fire on the historical v12.2 wording (see docs/claim_verification.md).

claims.note: THE historical failure. At v12.2 this claim was asserted in the deposited JOSS paper while all ten register entries were unsigned scaffolds. This check is the automated form of the `grep SCAFFOLD` that finally caught it; verification/retro_test.sh proves the detector still fires on a verbatim copy of that historical prose.

claims.claim: No living document states, without qualification, that predictions, register entries or scorecards are signed.
claims.note: The signing detector above targets 'cryptographically signed', 'signed and time-stamped' and 'signed before'. Plain statements such as 'the prediction is signed' or 'reproducers can sign scorecards' survived in the long-form methodology paper until the 20.0 deposit review. Kept as a separate claim so the negative control's calibrated count (18 historical sites) keeps its meaning; tests/test_verification.py requires this pattern to fire on the historical fixture too.

claims.claim: The register contains N pre-registered predictions (N stated in prose must match the register).
claims.note: Catches count drift as the register grows. The 8 -> 10 drift (v12.1/v12.2 added P9, P10) survived in fourteen places until the July 2026 audit found it by hand. v12.7 liveness fix: the number-word alternation stopped at 'twelve', so from the moment the register reached thirteen (P13, v12.6) this check matched zero prose sites and passed vacuously — a silently-dead check of exactly the class the retro-guard's MIN_SITES floor exists to catch. The alternation now runs to 'twenty' and `min_sites: 1` makes zero matched sites a FAILURE for every count claim. Extended at the reorganization to also match 'N worked examples': the deposited methodology paper still said 'ten worked examples' when the register held thirteen, a count claim the earlier pattern could not see. Extended again before the 20.0 deposit: 'ten near-term cosmological predictions' (the long-form methodology paper's abstract) and 'all 10 predictions' (its JOSS submission guide) escaped the qualifier list.

claims.claim: Every verdict a living document states for a prediction (PASS, FAIL, SUB-THRESHOLD) matches that prediction's scorecard.
claims.note: Verdicts change when a rule or a parameter is corrected: P1 and P4 both went from FAIL to PASS (the canonical parameter moved inside the region public data allow; the registered |z| < 3 rule was restored in scorers that had tightened it). Three documents still stated the old verdicts at the 20.0 deposit review. Registered statements and scorecards are out of scope (frozen records), and PREDICTIONS.md is generated and checked by predictions-table-current. A verdict word applies to the prediction IDs in its clause ('P1, P3 FAIL; P5 PASS') or directly after it ('a FAIL on P4'); lines describing the past are hedged by the `unless` list.

claims.claim: The publication strategy comprises N papers (N stated in prose must match papers/ on disk).
claims.note: Paper E was added after the 'four-paper strategy' phrasing was written. CHANGELOG.md is excluded by design: it is a historical record, and per project policy history is annotated rather than rewritten — a v12.0 entry describing the then-current four-paper strategy is accurate as history.

claims.claim: N scoring pipelines are active (N stated in prose must match scripts/predictions_score_P*.py).
Each scorecard records the SHA-256 of the pipeline output it scored, so the evidence chain is verifiable.
claims.note: Exact, mechanical: recomputes each hash. Catches a scorecard drifting from the output it claims to describe.

claims.claim: Every registered pipeline output names a JSON schema that exists, and validates against it.
claims.note: Until the 20.0 reorganization this claim was checked only by resolving each schema name to a file: the manifest said 'schema-validated' while nothing validated. The validator implements the draft-07 keywords the schemas use and reports any other keyword as an error instead of ignoring it (a fallback validator in earlier releases silently skipped numeric bounds). min_checked is a liveness floor.

claims.claim: No surviving claim that GSC explains a real observational anomaly (all such claims were retracted).
claims.note: The v12.0 release claimed the neutron-lifetime anomaly was explained; v12.1 retracted it. This keeps the retraction enforced. Broadened before the 20.0 deposit: the long-form methodology paper still said the P3 prediction 'explains the existing ~9-second beam-trap discrepancy', a phrasing the original pattern did not cover. tests/test_verification.py requires the pattern to catch that sentence in the historical fixture.

claims.claim: Citation metadata points at the canonical public repository.
claims.note: Guards against citing a private repo (a 404 for anyone following the citation), which was true until July 2026.

claims.claim: The theory document has a section for every prediction in the register.
claims.note: The highest documented prediction number must equal the register size.

claims.claim: CI asserts the register's prediction count without hardcoding it, so the assertion cannot drift as predictions are added.
claims.note: CI derives the expected count from predictions/P*/prediction.md; a hard-coded count once drifted and turned CI red.

claims.claim: The package's CI workflow contains no hard-wired version-directory working paths, so it runs unchanged whether the package sits at a repository root or in a subdirectory.
claims.note: Two past incidents: a repository sync overwrote a customized workflow, and a layout-specific workflow silently stopped triggering. The workflow detects the package directory at runtime instead.

claims.claim: No registered prediction pipeline instantiates the v10.1 coasting toy history (PowerLawHistory) — the canonical metrology exponent must never be used as an expansion-history exponent.
claims.note: Added v12.7 after the P8 finding: the same symbol p fed two incompatible models (T2 metrology exponent in P1/P2/P4/P5/P9; whole expansion law in P8 via PowerLawHistory). At p = 6e-4 the latter is a coasting universe excluded at >100 sigma by the bundled DESI BAO. The count/hash/schema checks could not see a cross-pipeline PHYSICAL inconsistency; this claim encodes the one lesson mechanically. The P8 pipeline keeps a loudly-named provenance option that imports the toy lazily inside a function; the pattern above targets instantiation at module scope or in default code paths — the provenance path constructs the class through a local import and is exercised only by an explicit flag.

claims.claim: No surviving claim that GSC predicts a redshift-drift sign flip / positive drift at z >= 2 relative to LCDM (withdrawn in v12.7: it was a toy-history artefact).
claims.note: Keeps the v12.7 withdrawal enforced across every prose surface, the same way no-unqualified-explained-anomaly keeps the v12.1 retraction enforced.

claims.claim: Every repository path mentioned in a living document exists in this package (no references to files of other versions or to moved files).
claims.note: The standalone guarantee made mechanical. CHANGELOG.md is excluded because its prehistory section describes the past; verification/fixtures/ is out of scope by glob (verbatim historical text). The `allow` list enumerates, one by one, the modules that registered statements P1–P7 name in their pipeline sections but that were planned and never built; each such entry carries an editorial flag, and OPEN_PROBLEMS.md problem 6 records the issue. The list is explicit on purpose: a pattern-based exemption would be the over-hedging the negative control exists to prevent. Two further entries are not modules: GSC_Framework.md is the former name of THEORY.md, listed on purpose in METHOD.md's table of names used inside frozen records, and paper.pdf and paper.tex are outputs of the renders that papers/paper_D_methodology/joss/SUBMIT.md tells the reader how to produce. Bare file names are checked since the 20.0 deposit review, which found three operator scripts, a dependency file and a linter named in living documents but absent from the package.

claims.claim: predictions/MANIFEST.sha256 lists the SHA-256 of every registered statement and output, and every listed file matches.
claims.note: The manifest is what gets quoted in each public deposit's description, so the deposit's date independently timestamps the exact register content.

claims.claim: PREDICTIONS.md is exactly what the generator produces from the register (the table cannot drift from the data).
Prediction pipelines are deterministic: identical inputs produce byte-identical output.
The joint CMB + BAO fit behind OPEN_PROBLEMS.md problems 1, 4 and 5 reproduces its committed numbers.
claims.note: Slow (one to two minutes): every fit is recomputed and compared with analyses/joint_fit.json within a relative tolerance of 0.2%, and analyses/joint_fit.md must be the rendering of the committed numbers. Requires --include-slow.

claims.claim: The coupled-black-hole fit behind OPEN_PROBLEMS.md problem 10 reproduces its committed numbers.
claims.note: Slow (about half a minute): every fit is recomputed and compared with analyses/ccbh_fit.json within 0.2%. Requires --include-slow.
